The model uses Bradley-Terry win probabilities reparameterized via logit transformation, with variance updating governed by a closed-form expression involving a reduction factor A and lower bound B. This allows for more responsive uncertainty quantification in dynamic environments like tennis. The heterogeneous random walk introduces time-varying volatility, enhancing realism. Surface transfer rules extend this to multi-context settings, leveraging known correlations and standard deviations to propagate ratings across surfaces. These primitives form a coherent framework for Bayesian uncertainty modeling in player performance evaluation.
